system.name: ADEPT
system.one_liner: Agentic speech-emotion recognition with probing tools; this figure shows how primary and minor emotion labels are built from five annotators' votes.

content.variant_note: two example cards, each with a vote bar above a grey traditional-label lane and a gold proposed-label lane; no arrows
content.argues: Plurality-based primary-plus-minor labels keep ties and minority votes that traditional single-label voting discards as 'No Agreement' or reduces to one label.
content.subject: Two annotation examples: five annotators' emotion votes and the labels derived from them by the traditional and the proposed scheme.

lessons.what_to_learn: Give each category one colour and keep it from the raw votes to every derived label, so a labelling rule can be read off the chips without arrows; a grey versus gold lane pair then shows what the old rule loses on the same votes.
lessons.suits: Annotation, labelling or aggregation rules explained on two or three toy cases, where the point is what the old rule discards or collapses.

evidence: preserving both tied primary emotions and minority-vote minor emotions
we employ a flexible Plurality-based Consensus strategy (Figure 1). Unlike strict majority rules, our approach explicitly models ambiguity
Is any of these emotions the primary emotion in the audio? If not, select Other and specify the emotion

summary: ADEPT turns a speech LLM into an agent that probes semantic and acoustic evidence before judging emotion, and it treats minority annotations as signal rather than noise. Figure 1 explains the label construction behind that. A grey box at the top quotes the MSP-Podcast survey question with its nine options. Below, two dashed-framed example cards each show five annotators' votes as colour-coded chips on a black bar (orange Happiness, green Neutral, red Surprise), then a grey Traditional Label lane next to a gold Proposed Label lane. In example 1 the old rule keeps only Happiness while the new one adds Neutral and Surprise as minor emotions; in example 2 a 2-2-1 tie is 'No Agreement (typically discarded)' but becomes two tied primaries plus one minor emotion. No arrows are used.
summary_zh: ADEPT 把语音大模型变成会调用探针工具的情感推理智能体。图 1 说明 MSP-Podcast 的标签构造：顶部是调查问题，两个示例用彩色标签条展示五位标注者的投票，对比灰色传统单标签与金色主次情感新标签，平局和少数票得以保留。
notes: Prior label kept (side-by-side-contrast, paired-lanes) and worked-walkthrough added because two concrete vote patterns are carried to labels. The paper text near the figure is cut off at 'Primary Emotion is defined as the class(es)', so the exact rule (plurality classes including ties are primary, other voted classes are minor) is read from the two examples and the caption. The figure contains no arrows and no pictures.
